---
title: Eligibility
---

::: {.callout-warning title="Attention"}
We tried to comply to the eligibility rules as best as we could in our
registration form but we reserve the rights to refuse/stop participation of
teams from countries/companies subject to restrictions at any stage of the
challenge.
:::


## Eligibility for Participation

The inscription form already implements, as far as possible, the restrictions
for the origin of participating teams.

The restrictions are mainly about teams originating or affiliated to
institutions/companies from (non \acr{ECTL}) countries subject to sanctions.  
Despite the reason for the sanctions, the practical limitation for us is the
impossibility to transfer funds to the winners if based in these countries.

A thematic map of target countries is available at <https://www.sanctionsmap.eu/>.


## Eligibility for Prize

The winning submissions/solutions will only be eligible for the awards if

* the team is NOT related to sanctioned countries
* external datasets are openly accessible/usable and documented.
* all **source code** will be made openly available
  on GitHub under the **GNU GPLv3 license**.  
  (It will then be forked by the Challenge GitHub account for organizational
  purposes.)
* all **additional data sets** used are openly available
  under an open source license.
* sufficient **documentation** is provided **to understand and reproduce** the results.
* the solution is **_original_**: teams must use their own original solutions.
  Re-using any existing implementation is only allowed if the original authors 
  grant you the rights to use their solution and if you made significant
  modifications to the algorithm or model.
  In particular, simply re-using existing code and rewriting the data input and 
  output mechanism is not sufficient. Adding parameters to the model and 
  modifying filters to match the specific peculiarities of the data, however,
  can be considered sufficient.
